facts.label: Relativa sem pronome + will
facts.sub: The tent we shared was tiny. The photos I took are on my laptop. I’ll never forget it. After will, use the base verb.

facts.label: Sem pronome
facts.sub: Quando o substantivo é objeto, you pode tirar that/which: the tent (that) we shared, the photos (that) I took. Fica mais natural e curto. Não repita o objeto com it.

facts.label: Com sujeito
facts.sub: Se o substantivo é o sujeito do segundo verbo, o pronome fica: a woman who cooked, a tent that leaked. Teste: se há um sujeito depois do substantivo, pode tirar o pronome.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We can say “the tent we shared” without that.
We can say “the man worked here” for “the man who worked”.
items.why: With a subject, we need who or that.

items.s: Will + never is common for strong memories.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We can say “the tent we shared” without that. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We can say “the man worked here” for “the man who worked”. → Falso (With a subject, we need who or that.)
Will + never is common for strong memories. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Memories of a camping holiday · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet evening in Leeds, in the north of England. Carl and Dan look at old photos on a screen. Last summer they went camping in the hills. The trip had rain, laughter and a few small problems. Now every photo brings back a story. They talk about the days they’ll always remember.

“Dan, that camping trip is a holiday I’ll never forget.” says Carl. “Me too! The tent we shared was tiny, and I’ll remember the cold nights.” says Dan. “The backpack you carried was so heavy that I still laugh about it.” says Carl.
